system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

exchanges.user:
ISSUES:
- SPA-N-001 | General liability cap | seller's draft: 20% / AUD 4,800,000 general cap
- SPA-N-002 | De minimis & basket | seller's draft: Raised de minimis / aggregate basket
- SPA-N-003 | General claims time limit | seller's draft: 18-month general notice period
- SPA-N-004 | Fundamental/Title regime | seller's draft: Blur fundamental into general regime
- SPA-N-005 | Fraud carve-out | seller's draft: Subject fraud to contractual limits
- SPA-N-006 | Disclosure scope | seller's draft: Whole-data-room / public-register deemed disclosure (disclosure letter §1.1-1.2)
- SPA-N-007 | Buyer knowledge qualifier | seller's draft: Blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion
- SPA-N-008 | Bluefen consent | seller's draft: Consent treated as obtained on delivery; ~AUD 3,600,000 (30% FY26 rev). AUD 75k payment unverified.
- SPA-N-009 | Riverlark facility | seller's draft: Post-completion release acceptable; ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding
- SPA-N-010 | Employee bonuses | seller's draft: AUD 420,000 closing bonuses excluded from funds flow (DD-005)
- SPA-N-011 | Ironquay IP indemnity | seller's draft: Narrow indemnity; DD-004/DD-010 AUD 180,000 open, SOW3 transfer conditioned on payment
- SPA-N-012 | Export/privacy incident | seller's draft: DD-006 incident, ~1,240 records to unintended address; preliminary
- SPA-N-013 | Sandbar renewals | seller's draft: Three renewals AUD 110,000 each = AUD 330,000 aggregate
- SPA-N-014 | Category separation | seller's draft: General regime overriding specific categories
- SPA-N-015 | Title verification | seller's draft: DD-012 share register offered as proof of title
- SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | seller's draft: Assume resolved / unlimited or general treatment

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
Seller’s assertions that terms are “market”, agreed or “FINAL” are not evidence of Buyer approval. The positions below are Buyer proposals, based on the extracts supplied; the full SPA and underlying DD records remain to be checked.

| Issue | Seller’s position | What Buyer should want | Recommendation and one-line reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| **SPA-N-001: General liability cap** | 20% of price: **AUD 4.8m**. | A materially higher general warranty cap, with separate treatment for fundamental warranties, tax, specific indemnities and fraud. | **Reopen; propose 50% (AUD 12m)** as a negotiating starting point—not a market assertion—because 20% may leave substantial acquisition risk with Buyer. |
| **SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket** | Claims must exceed **AUD 25,000**; **AUD 250,000 deductible basket**, recovering only the excess. | Lower thresholds; a tipping basket recovering all qualifying claims once crossed; aggregation of related claims; exclusions for protected categories. | **Propose AUD 10,000 de minimis and AUD 120,000 tipping basket**, with related-claim aggregation, because the present combination excludes smaller losses and permanently deducts AUD 250,000. |
| **SPA-N-003: General claims time limit** | General warranties: **18 months**; limitations extend to all Claims unless expressly excluded. | At least **24 months** for general warranties; longer category-specific periods; timely notified claims survive expiry without an onerous proceedings deadline. | **Seek 24 months and reject blanket application**, because issues may emerge only through subsequent reporting cycles. |
| **SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime** | Capacity and title share the general cap and deadline. | Separate fundamental warranties covering capacity, ownership, valid issuance and unencumbered transfer; no basket/de minimis; at least a price-level cap and longer survival. | **Seek a 100% price cap and six-year contractual notification period**, subject to execution/statutory review, because defective title can undermine the entire acquisition. |
| **SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out** | Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to all Claims; no express fraud exception is shown. | Express protection for fraud and fraudulent misrepresentation, including appropriate attribution to Seller; preservation of non-excludable rights. | **Carve fraud out of caps, thresholds, deadlines, disclosure/knowledge defences, exclusive remedy and non-reliance**, because boilerplate should not shelter fraudulent conduct. |
| **SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope** | Blanket disclosure of the data room, referenced material, accounts, registers and public records. | Only fair disclosure with sufficient detail to identify the nature and scope of the exception, preferably against specific warranties; a fixed, accessible disclosure bundle. | **Reject blanket deemed disclosure and require specific, intelligible disclosures**, because document availability alone does not adequately identify an accepted risk. |
| **SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier** | No claim for matters known by Buyer or advisers, including anything discoverable from data room/public records. | Delete the exclusion; fallback limited to actual knowledge of named Buyer individuals, without constructive or adviser-imputed knowledge. | **Delete or tightly narrow, preserving specific indemnities**, because “discoverable” transfers diligence risk wholesale to Buyer. |
| **SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent** | Reasonable endeavours; condition satisfied by delivery of written consent, although no final consent or satisfaction evidence is supplied. | Buyer-waivable completion condition requiring effective consent and satisfaction of clause 11.3 conditions, without unacceptable changes; verification before closing. | **Do not close until consent and associated conditions are verified**, because approximately **30% of FY26 revenue** depends on this relationship. |
| **SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility** | Approximately **AUD 3.2m** outstanding; security release follows Completion. | Verified payout, lender change-control treatment and binding discharge arrangements effective at Completion; debt deducted in the funds flow without double counting. | **Require simultaneous repayment and effective release backed by lender undertakings**, because a debt-free/cash-free acquisition must not leave Buyer exposed to Seller’s financing/security. |
| **SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses** | **AUD 420,000** conditional closing bonuses treated as Seller’s matter and omitted from funds flow; on-costs unspecified. | Seller bears transaction-triggered bonuses and applicable payroll tax, superannuation and other on-costs, with appropriate payment/accrual arrangements. | **Quantify and include as a Seller-funded deduction or payment, with a shortfall indemnity**, because omission can leave the acquired company funding Seller’s transaction costs. |
| **SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity** | Indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment; **AUD 180,000** recorded open, with no payment receipt or confirmatory assignment. | Verified payment and effective assignment before Completion; indemnity for ownership defects, third-party claims, remediation and resulting losses, under a separate regime. | **Require documentary cure and broaden the indemnity beyond the invoice**, because paying an invoice alone does not establish clean ownership or cover the consequences of defective title. |
| **SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident** | Described as preliminary and unlikely material; access, scope, notification requirements and loss remain unresolved. | Prompt investigation, containment and legal assessment; required notifications/remediation; updates and a specific indemnity for attributable pre-Completion exposure. | **Keep open, investigate and allocate residual risk expressly**, because uncertainty is neither proof of a reportable breach nor a basis for dismissing exposure. |
| **SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals** | Three **AUD 110,000** renewals—**AUD 330,000 aggregate**—called ordinary-course operating costs. | Review together for timing, scope, necessity, termination rights and accounting treatment; Buyer approval for material new commitments before Completion. | **Verify classification before agreeing treatment**, because neither automatic Seller deduction nor ordinary-course treatment is justified on the supplied facts. |
| **SPA-N-014: Category separation** | Broad limitations and remedy provisions apply to all Claims unless expressly displaced. | Separate regimes for general warranties, fundamental warranties, tax, specific indemnities, covenants, price adjustments and fraud, with clear precedence. | **Rewrite definitions, exclusions and cross-references across clauses 9.3, 12, 13 and 20.5**, because an all-Claims provision could silently defeat negotiated protections. |
| **SPA-N-015: Title verification** | Relies on DD-012 share register showing Seller holds 100%. | Independent reconciliation of issued capital, allotment/transfer history, certificates, constitution, options/conversion rights and encumbrances; valid completion transfer documentation. | **Verify rather than accept the register as conclusive**, because recorded ownership alone does not establish valid, unencumbered title to all equity. |
| **SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms** | Tax and IP considered settled within the general warranty regime. | Separate pre-Completion tax indemnity and tax warranties with survival aligned to assessment exposure; robust IP ownership/licensing warranties and tailored protection for known defects. | **Expressly reserve both categories and negotiate scope, caps and survival separately**, because tax liabilities and core software ownership risks may emerge beyond the general warranty period and cap. |

**Completion priorities:** Bluefen consent, Riverlark discharge, bonus funding, Ironquay ownership cure and title verification. Keep the incident investigation and renewal classification open pending evidence; disclosure does not itself resolve or allocate those risks.
=== END ADVICE ===
